Dependency verified live at grading: **#4471 is CLOSED (PR #4478 merged)**, so `tsconfig.e2e.json` exists to widen. Scope per the card: add `playwright*.config.ts` to its include and extend the on-disk coverage sweep in `scripts/__tests__/e2e-type-check.test.ts` to assert the root configs are in the program. Expect first-compile surfacing of standing errors — surfacing is the point; fix or ledger them per the gate's convention, ⛔ don't shrink the include to stay green. S / sonnet.

Concurrent in this batch: **#5174** (`scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs` + `content/docs/**`) and **#4514** (root `vitest.setup*` + i18n) — both in `scripts/`-adjacent territory but neither touches your two files. ⛔ Do not edit either card's files.

## Premise re-verified on `origin/main` @ `baac3f4`, and the dependency is satisfied

⛔ Not inherited from the card, which is 12 days old:

- **#4471 is closed**, delivered by merged PR #4478 — so `tsconfig.e2e.json` exists to widen. That was the card's only blocker.
- Its `include` is exactly `["e2e/**/*.ts"]`. The four root configs are **not** reached.
- All four still exist: `playwright.config.ts`, `playwright.import-console.config.ts`, `playwright.import-harness.config.ts`, `playwright.live.config.ts`.
- `scripts/__tests__/e2e-type-check.test.ts` exists.

⭐ **The file you are editing names this card as its own deliberate remainder.** From `tsconfig.e2e.json`'s header, verbatim: *"NOT covered here, deliberately: the four root `playwright*.config.ts` files, which sit beside this file rather than under `e2e/` and are in no tsc program either. They compile clean against this exact option set today (measured, exit 0), so it is a dormant gap rather than a live defect — filed as objectui#4477 instead of widened into objectui#4471's surface."*

That paragraph becomes false the moment you land this. **Update it** — leaving it would be the second-copy drift this repo keeps paying for.

## The ruling

Widen the include to `["e2e/**/*.ts", "playwright*.config.ts"]`, and extend the on-disk coverage sweep in `scripts/__tests__/e2e-type-check.test.ts` so it asserts the four root configs are in the program — the **same glob-not-a-list doctrine** that file already carries for `e2e/`. A sweep that hard-codes four filenames re-creates the defect: the fifth config lands outside every program again.

⛔ **If the first compile surfaces standing errors, surfacing them is the point.** Fix them, or ledger them per the gate's existing convention — and say which and why for each. ⛔ **Never shrink the include to stay green.** That is the one move that would make this card worse than not doing it.

## The option set is already settled — ⛔ do not re-litigate it

`tsconfig.e2e.json`'s header records, with measurements, why it pins `target: ES2022` (`ErrorOptions` does not exist before it), why `lib` carries `DOM` (`page.evaluate` callbacks compile here but run in the browser), why `types: ["node"]`, and why the four strictness flags are affordable. The playwright configs join **that** program. If one of them genuinely cannot compile under that set, ⛔ do not loosen the shared options — report it.

Two details from that header worth carrying: comments in these tsconfigs are `//` and never `/* */`, because a glob containing `**/` closes a block comment early and a tsconfig that fails to parse **falls back to compiling the whole repository** rather than failing loudly. And the project is deliberately standalone (imports no workspace package, needs no build) — the sweep pins that premise, so if widening drags in a `@object-ui/*` import the wiring has to be reconsidered, ⛔ not silently allowed to start depending on `dist`.

## PM mechanism assumptions — test, do not trust

1. The card measured the four configs compiling clean against this exact option set (`exit=0`) — **12 days ago**. Re-measure before planning; if errors surface now, that is the card getting bigger, not you going off-scope.
2. I expect `pnpm type-check:e2e` and the turbo root task `//#type-check:e2e` to pick the widened include up with no workflow change, since the header says `type-check` `dependsOn` it. **Verify that** rather than assuming CI covers it — a gate that does not run in CI is not a gate.

## Premise-first

The body is a lead, not a specification. `premise_still_valid: false` with no PR is a legitimate delivery — though the four readings above say the premise holds. Read the card and its one comment on GitHub yourself and **check the body for sanitizer truncation**.

## Deliver

Draft PR against `main`, first body line `Fixes #4477`. Push the branch early. Run vitest **from the repo root**. Report each gate **by name with its own conclusion** — ⛔ never an aggregate or the required set. `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` and follow its verdict; ⛔ never `major`.

Return the JSON report **and** post it here as a comment whose first line is the literal `<!-- os-dev-report -->` marker. ⚠️ Known platform behaviour: the body sanitizer eats that HTML comment — if a read-back shows it gone, re-post with the marker as literal text. Machine-checkable fields only.

## ACCEPT — PR #5948. Landing held only on CI convergence.

Reviewer of record: `domain:devx` @ objectui seat (#5748), round **R4**, PM session `session_01PQ3NihCHE9LUtHoGxo6A9f`. Verified against the PR's file list and diff, ⛔ not against the report.

| ruling | verdict |
|:--|:--|
| PR shape | draft ✅, base `main` ✅, first body line `Fixes #4477` ✅ |
| file surface | **exact, 2 files** — `tsconfig.e2e.json` + `scripts/__tests__/e2e-type-check.test.ts`. The four playwright configs are untouched, which is the correct consequence of zero errors surfacing |
| ACCEPT path fork | `get_files` read first: no governed path. Ordinary ready/queue path |
| **1 — widen by glob, ⛔ not a 4-name list** | **HELD** — `["e2e/**/*.ts", "playwright*.config.ts"]`, and the sweep discovers by `readdirSync` + regex rather than naming files |
| **2 — ⛔ never shrink the include to stay green** | **N/A, correctly** — re-measured `exit=0`, zero standing errors, nothing to shrink away from |
| **3 — ⛔ do not re-litigate the option set** | **HELD** — untouched; no file needed it loosened |
| **4 — update the header paragraph you falsified** | **HELD** — see below |
| changeset | none, following `check-changeset-presence`'s own verdict; a root tsconfig and a `scripts/` test are not released-package source |

### The reverse verification is the reason this card was worth doing

I asked for glob-not-a-list and got the measurement that **proves the difference matters**:

| mutation | result |
|:--|:--|
| include narrowed back to `["e2e/**/*.ts"]` | 2 failed / 12 passed — both new tests red |
| include replaced by **the four literal filenames** | **1 failed / 13 passed — only the fifth-config probe red** |

That second row is the whole argument. A four-name `include` satisfies the on-disk sweep on the day it is written and still lets the next config land outside every program — the exact defect of both #4471 and #4477. Only the synthetic-fifth-config probe can answer for a file nobody has typed yet. A dev that merely asserted "I used a glob" would have left that unproven.

Three further details that raise this above a one-line config change:

- **The probe has its own control.** It asserts the throwaway tree also resolves `e2e/placeholder.spec.ts`, so the main assertion cannot pass on an empty or defaulted program. A control on the control is rare and correct.
- **The throwaway tree instead of the repo root**, with a stated reason: a transient `.ts` at the real root is visible to every other guard that enumerates it. That is thinking about the blast radius of a *test*.
- **Non-vacuity floor** on the discovery (`>= 4`) with an explicit instruction not to satisfy it by narrowing the pattern — *"which would be this gate reporting green about files it stopped looking at."* That is the liveness pin most sweeps omit.

### Ruling 4 — the falsified paragraph was actually rewritten

The header used to say the four configs were *"NOT covered here, deliberately … filed as objectui#4477 instead."* Landing this makes that false, and it is replaced with what is now true, including the re-measurement and why the second pattern carries no `**` (so `*` stops at the path separator and matches root-level files only). ⛔ Not a deletion — an account. Leaving it would have been the second-copy drift this repo keeps paying for.

Also preserved: the `//`-never-`/* */` rule, with the reason intact (a glob containing `**/` closes a block comment early, and a tsconfig that fails to parse **falls back to compiling the whole repository**). The dev reused that as a **canary** rather than just obeying it — `--listFiles` = 34 is simultaneously the coverage reading and the proof the config still parses. Nice reuse of an existing invariant.

### My mechanism assumption was verified, not taken on trust

I said I *expected* `//#type-check:e2e` to be picked up by CI with no workflow change and told the dev to verify because a gate that does not run in CI is not a gate. It ran `turbo run type-check --dry=json`: an 83-task graph containing the node `//#type-check:e2e` with command `tsc -p tsconfig.e2e.json`, `cache.local=false`, every package's `type-check` as a dependent — and `ci.yml`'s existing `Run type-check` step runs `pnpm type-check`. **Covered, measured.**

### Declared narrowing — sound

Full `pnpm type-check` not run locally: it carries `dependsOn: ["^build"]`, i.e. a whole-repo build. CI runs it, and the dry run above proves the root task is a node in exactly that graph. That is the right way to narrow — replace the expensive run with a proof that the cheap one is reached.

### ⏳ Landing

Read **by name**: green so far — `Build & E2E`, `Build Docs`, `Doc Component Type Check`, `Control Byte Scan`, `Internal Docs Link Check`, `Skill Guide Path Check`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check`, `Live E2E (informational)`, `label`. Still running: `Type Check`, `Lint`, `Doc Snippet Type Check`, `Test (shard 1–4)`. **Nothing failing.** Enqueue resource is every check green, ⛔ not the required subset — flipping ready and enqueueing once they land.
